goal.text: Yeah is an Emacs Lisp agent harness: the user's Emacs session is itself the runtime of the agent; every call to the model goes through gptel, every tool goes through the registry and the permission system, and the session log stays append-only

claims.subject: every file under lib/ byte-compiles without errors and without warnings
claims.falsifier: the byte-compilation of lib/ fails, or reports a warning

claims.subject: the agent loop is a finite state machine with exactly twelve states and twenty transitions: the machine can run one model turn and be asked again, and it can record a turn that failed
claims.falsifier: the state list or the transition table has a different length, a transition is missing, or the machine cannot return to the model
claims.control: sed -i 's/^    interrupted$/    completed-tmp/; s/^    completed$/    interrupted/; s/^    completed-tmp$/    completed/' lib/yeah-state.el

claims.subject: the session log is append-only: a record that has been written is never rewritten and never removed
claims.falsifier: an earlier record is missing from the file after a later append

claims.subject: compaction is a projection: the source records stay on disk and the compaction record joins them
claims.falsifier: a source record disappears from the log when the compaction runs

claims.subject: a tool call is refused when the number of arguments, or the type of one of them, does not match the tool's declared input
claims.falsifier: a call with the wrong number of arguments, or with an argument of the wrong type, is accepted

claims.subject: the permission system decides by the last matching rule, and asks when nothing matches
claims.falsifier: an earlier matching rule overrides a later one, or the default stops being ask
claims.control: sed -i 's/(setq last-match rule)/(unless last-match (setq last-match rule))/' lib/yeah-perm.el

claims.subject: the ACP dispatcher answers initialize, session/new, session/load, session/prompt and session/cancel, answers a prompt with a stop reason, and refuses a method it does not know
claims.falsifier: one of the methods is unrouted, a prompt is answered without a stop reason, or an unknown method is answered instead of refused

claims.subject: the emcp registry and schemas/emcp-v1.json name the same tools, describe them the same way, publish the same read-only set, and a duplicate id is refused
claims.falsifier: the registry and the schema name, describe or publish different tools, or a duplicate id is accepted

claims.subject: every tick's changes can be undone: an undo boundary is taken around the buffer or the file the tick touched
claims.falsifier: a change made inside the boundary is not recorded in the undo list

claims.subject: no module installs global gptel hooks; lib/yeah-gptel.el configures each request privately without changing global gptel state
claims.falsifier: any module installs or removes a global gptel hook instead of passing private request options

claims.subject: a sub-agent spawns a child session, waits for it, and a spawn past the depth limit is refused
claims.falsifier: the child session is not created, or the depth limit is not enforced

claims.subject: the Yeah shell keeps a bounded history of what was sent to it, and creates its REPL buffer
claims.falsifier: the history is unbounded, or the REPL buffer is not created

claims.subject: the tick, the permission system, the tool registry and the session log are wired into one loop: each is called from outside its own module
claims.falsifier: a module of the loop is called only from inside itself

claims.subject: experimental PTC is disabled by default and is not a security boundary; when explicitly enabled for trusted code, direct and higher-order calls outside its restricted core are refused before evaluation
claims.falsifier: disabled PTC evaluates a form, a normal enabled registry tool is rejected, or a forbidden direct/higher-order form executes an outside effect

claims.subject: the model is called through the private gptel adapter and nowhere else: one function in one module is the whole of the transport, and it speaks gptel's supported request shape
claims.falsifier: a second module calls the model directly, the call site does not exist, or the transport does not reach gptel with the prompt and the callback

claims.subject: the ACP agent speaks JSON-RPC over stdio: a client can open the process and exchange an initialize request, a session/new request and their answers
claims.falsifier: a client cannot exchange a JSON-RPC message with the agent over stdio

claims.subject: one turn asks the model, dispatches the tool calls the model asked for through the permission system and the registry, writes what happened into the log, and asks the model again until it asks for nothing
claims.falsifier: a tool call the model asked for is not dispatched, or is dispatched without the rules deciding, or the results do not reach the log

claims.subject: the tool calls of one answer of the model run together: a shared tool may run alongside the other shared tools, an exclusive tool runs alone, and the batch settles only when every call has settled
claims.falsifier: two shared calls of one answer run one after the other, an exclusive call runs while another is running, or the batch continues before its last call has settled

claims.subject: every step of a run is a typed record of the log: what the model asked, what the rules answered, what the tool did, and what the model said, and a record carries the fields its type declares
claims.falsifier: the log holds a record of an unknown type, a record whose fields are not the ones its type declares, or a step of the run that leaves no record
claims.control: sed -i 's/(unless (yeah-events--same-fields-p declared given)/(unless t (yeah-events--same-fields-p declared given)/' lib/yeah-events.el

claims.subject: the interface reads the event stream and nothing else: it shows the transcript, the tool calls and their state, the approvals that are still waiting, and what the run has cost
claims.falsifier: the view cannot be built from the log, or it shows a run that differs from what the log says

claims.subject: an approval is answered once, always or reject, and a run with nobody at the keyboard answers by the policy: the rules allow what they name and refuse everything else
claims.falsifier: an answer that is not one of the three is accepted, an answer of always is not written into the rules, or a run with nobody at the keyboard asks a question it cannot answer

claims.subject: the context of a run is counted, an overflow is seen, the summary is written by the model and not by a placeholder, and the outputs of old tools are pruned without leaving the log
claims.falsifier: the summary is not the one the model wrote, an overflow is not seen, or a pruned record is no longer a record

claims.subject: the sessions of a project can be listed, every one of them says what it cost, and a run can be continued from a point that is not the end without the rest of the line disappearing
claims.falsifier: the index does not name the sessions, the cost of a run is unknown, or the branch loses the path that was abandoned
claims.control: sed -i 's/(push record abandoned)/(push record path)/' lib/yeah-sessions.el

claims.subject: a call that fails is tried again, a call that hangs is cut, a run that repeats itself is stopped, and none of it holds the main loop
claims.falsifier: a failing call is not tried again, a hanging call is not cut, a repeated call is not seen, or the call waits in the main loop

claims.subject: the emacs tool namespace is served over stdio: a client can initialize, list the published tools and call one of them, and the published set is the read-only set of the registry
claims.falsifier: a client cannot list or call the published tools, or the published set drifts from the registry

claims.subject: Yeah connects to a foreign MCP server over stdio, lists its tools, imports them into its own registry under a namespaced name, and calls them through the same permission system as local tools
claims.falsifier: a foreign tool is not imported into the registry, or it is imported under a name that does not carry the server, or the call does not reach the foreign server

claims.subject: the same kernel runs attached to a session, in its own Emacs as a service, and in batch, and the placement changes nothing but the answer to a question: the same task writes the same events in all three
claims.falsifier: a placement changes what the run wrote down, or the service cannot be started, or the batch placement has no exit code
claims.control: sed -i 's/(yeah-placement-batch prompt/(yeah-placement-batch (concat prompt " and something else")/' lib/yeah-placement.el

claims.subject: a run owns its permission rules: two runs in one Emacs do not share one truth, and the rules of a run decide before the person is asked
claims.falsifier: the rules of a run are the global rules, or a rule added by a run changes the rules of another run, or a request the rules do not decide is answered without the person

claims.subject: the bridge reaches the live buffers of an attached Emacs through emacsclient, and the tools it offers are approved separately: nothing enters the registry until the operator asks for it
claims.falsifier: the bridge calls the attached Emacs through a shell, or it hangs when the attached Emacs does not answer, or the bridge tools are in the registry before the operator asks for them

claims.subject: a sub-agent runs in its own session with its own context and its own permissions: a tool it was not granted is refused, the refusal is in its own journal, and its result comes back to the parent
claims.falsifier: a sub-agent shares the session of its parent, or it may use a tool it was not granted, or its result is lost

claims.subject: an agent preset is a file, not code: a header with a name, a description, a model and the tools it may use, and a body that is the prompt
claims.falsifier: a preset cannot be found, or its header is not read, or its body is read when the preset is only listed

claims.subject: the package exposes M-x yeah, M-x yeah-ask and M-x yeah-doctor, declares supported Emacs/gptel versions, and provides a package-vc bootstrap with no development-tool dependency
claims.falsifier: a product entry point is missing, package requirements are absent, or the bootstrap depends on mathc/Nix

claims.subject: malformed tool argument containers become a bounded tool failure and the turn completes
claims.falsifier: malformed args escape as an error, hang the turn, or produce a successful tool-end

claims.subject: a synchronous or asynchronous tool handler exception becomes a structured failure and the batch settles
claims.falsifier: a handler exception escapes the scheduler or leaves a pending call

claims.subject: every tool call settles at most once: a duplicate asynchronous callback is a no-op
claims.falsifier: a duplicate callback replaces the first result, decrements pending twice, or emits another tool-end

claims.subject: every model-facing tool result is a string or a structured error; nil and non-string results are normalized before logging and continuation
claims.falsifier: a nil or non-string result reaches the model, or a missing result is logged as success
claims.control: sed -i 's/(list :yeah-error "Error: tool produced no result")/nil/' lib/yeah-scheduler.el

claims.subject: the built-in coding tools perform an end-to-end project scenario: read/glob/grep, tick-guarded edit, Elisp validation, async bash and introspection
claims.falsifier: a built-in tool is missing, a guarded edit fails, a stale tick mutates a buffer, bash does not settle, or the final Elisp is unreadable

claims.subject: context overflow enters compacting and continues only after a nonblank asynchronous summary is committed; sources and pruning events remain in the append-only journal
claims.falsifier: the turn waits for the summary, skips compacting, commits an empty summary, or deletes source events

claims.subject: opening a session with a malformed or unterminated JSONL tail preserves valid records and exposes recovery metadata instead of silently discarding corruption
claims.falsifier: a malformed line has no recovery metadata or warning, or opening the session rewrites the damaged log

claims.subject: frozen inputs form a persistent bounded FIFO, steering is delivered at tool-batch boundaries, cancellation stops managed processes and late callbacks, and restart recovery is explicit
claims.falsifier: steering arrives between tools, a late callback changes a terminal run, pending work auto-executes after restart, or a managed process stays live after cancellation

claims.subject: completion nudges are visible and bounded, a whole-run deadline cancels the run, retries use backoff, and repeated read-only inspection is not a doom loop
claims.falsifier: nudges exceed their budget or are hidden, a deadline does not stop the run, retries are immediate, or repeated reads are treated as a loop
